No item text was shipped (BLOCKED), so there is no item_text<->item and no option_text<->resp mapping to verify; this row records what was ruled out so that 'couldn't check' does not read as 'checked'. Routes eliminated: 1 (per-item published statistics) - the only publication is closed access and publishes nothing per item; 2 (per-item response ranges) - all 16 codes share one 1-6 scale, per-item observed ranges are 1-5/2-6/1-6 etc. with no structural signature; 3 (published totals) - none published; 4 (a parameter the text implies) - no text; 5 (subscale blocks) - the PWI is scored as a single index, no published item->subscale map; 6 (keying polarity) - the PWI has no reverse-worded items; 9 (response-frequency matching) - the source stores integers, not labels, so there is nothing to count against. What WAS established and re-runs in verify_cognitive_load_klimova_2023_pwi.R (VERDICT: PASS): 16 codes PWICONTROLa..h / PWIEXPa..h; 170 respondents, 83 CONTROL-only, 87 EXP-only, 0 both (83+87=170, the paper's N); per-item n flat at 83 (CONTROL) and 87 (EXP); letterwise means CONTROL (a..h) 3.69 3.43 3.30 4.14 3.45 3.98 3.00 4.41 vs EXP 4.18 4.44 4.16 4.87 4.26 4.70 3.45 4.41, Pearson r = 0.761 over the 8 letters - i.e. two between-subjects label conditions of the same eight items. The one content-bearing signal found is negative: letter h means 4.41 (rank 8 of 8) in CONTROL and 4.41 (rank 5 of 8) in EXP, so h is NOT at the floor, which disfavours the reading in which the eighth PWI column is the optional spirituality/religion domain; the minimum is letter g (3.00 / 3.45). This route does NOT establish which PWI domain any letter refers to, does NOT choose between the two standard 8-column PWI compositions, does NOT fix the order within the seven core domains, and does NOT recover any of the six response-option labels - which is why the status is NO_ROUTE and not PARTIAL.

WHAT WAS CHECKED INSTEAD, and it is not a mapping (verify_cognitive_load_klimova_2023_stomp.R, VERDICT: PASS): (a) the CONTR/EXP suffix is the between-subjects labelling arm -- 170 ids, 747 CONTR rows, 783 EXP rows, 0 ids in both arms; (b) letter x denotes the same item in both arms -- matching each CONTR letter's full resp 1-6 frequency profile to each EXP letter's by total variation distance gives own-letter TVD 0.073-0.221 (mean 0.137) vs cross-letter 0.098-0.776 (mean 0.383), identity closest for 6 of 9 letters with the 3 misses losing by <= 0.045, and total identity TVD 1.229 against 20,000 random pairings (mean 3.207, min 1.452, p = 0.00005); (c) resp=6 behaves like an off-scale category rather than the top of a 6-point preference scale -- 0-18 uses per item out of 83-87, never used by 5 of the 18 items, 4.2% of all responses, while 1-5 are populated almost throughout. WHAT THIS DOES NOT ESTABLISH: which genre or wording letter a..i refers to, the response-option wording, the direction of the 1-5 scale, or the meaning of code 6 -- (b) pins only that the two arms share one item list, not what any item is. route: 6 (keying polarity), via exact reconstruction of the authors' SOCTOTAL
evidence: Reversing exactly {INVSOC1, INVSOC2, INVSOC3, INVSOC7, SOC10} (= SOC-13 items 1,2,3,7,10) reproduces the deposited SOCTOTAL for 921/921 respondents; it is the unique subset of all 8192 that does, the next best being {INVSOC1,INVSOC3,SOC4,INVSOC7,SOC10} at 255/921, {INVSOC1,INVSOC2,INVSOC3,INVSOC7,SOC10,SOC11} at 251/921 and {INVSOC1,INVSOC2,INVSOC3,INVSOC7} at 214/921. That set is exactly the canonical SOC-13 negatively worded set named in PMC8751372 (CC BY). Corroborated by item-rest correlations against the sum of the 8 positive items: INVSOC1 -0.307, INVSOC2 -0.257, INVSOC3 -0.294, INVSOC7 -0.296, SOC10 -0.463 versus SOC4 +0.314, SOC5 +0.343, SOC6 +0.492, SOC8 +0.543, SOC9 +0.609, SOC11 +0.346, SOC12 +0.597, SOC13 +0.609 -- 13/13 signs as predicted. Live item codes are identical to the source .sav column names (irw_table_sets, server-side). This does NOT distinguish items within a polarity class: nothing here separates SOC5 from SOC6 or INVSOC2 from INVSOC3, so a swap inside a class would go undetected. Route 5 (subscale block structure) was run and is non-diagnostic here rather than negative: only 5/13 items have their top-correlating partner in their own SOC-13 subscale and mean within-subscale r 0.268 vs between 0.235, consistent with PMC8751372's own finding that the 3-factor SOC-13 model fits poorly (CFI 0.649). Hence PARTIAL, not VERIFIED.

Route 6, keying polarity, run on live irw_fetch data (171 ids, 7523 rows). Mean within-domain correlation is POSITIVE for all 44 items: the 16 canonically reverse-keyed items span +0.117 (bfi41) to +0.528 (bfi21), the 28 forward-keyed items span +0.188 (bfi42) to +0.464 (bfi1); 0 of 16 negative where raw storage predicts 16 of 16 negative. This confirms the .sav labels' '(already reverse scored)' claim and justifies flipping those 16 items' anchors against the .sav value labels (labels18: 1=Strongly disagree..5=Strongly Agree). Semantic cross-check: bfi12 'Starts quarrels with others' stored mean 4.08 => raw endorsement 1.92, the expected floor in a healthy young-adult sample. WHAT THIS DOES NOT ESTABLISH: it pins the storage DIRECTION of every item, not item identity within a polarity class; identity rests on the .sav variable labels (mapping_basis=data_labels), so this route alone is PARTIAL.
